name: Lou Arnett
voice: I set the distance in a planning office. My father made me walk it with his groceries.
agenda: To walk the twenty paces with groceries before signing off.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an unlined tan jacket and a little coil of soft measuring tape. Lou has two dimples that appear only with a full smile, with a long plait tucked inside the collar. Lou looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry during a conversation.
life: “I learned transport planning on the bus I took to two part-time jobs.” Saturday often includes a stop at the entrance to the Wash House, where Lou stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
personality: Lou has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
family: Franklin Brandt is Lou’s stepsibling. Lou brings a spare shopping bag. Franklin chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *Spin cycle choir*, Franklin says, “I wanted the noisy bearing replaced. Hearing the song hasn't changed my mind about my night shift.”
connections: Agnes Kahn. The planner learns why the new morning light matters to a lip reader. Also in the story is Stella Hull (access reviewer).

name: Jamie Calloway
voice: Our porch got quieter. I miss knowing school is out by the sudden noise.
agenda: To keep one ordinary after-school sound in the house.
appearance: Jamie is easy to recognize by a loose dark braid and two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Usually dressed in a pale blue work shirt with a replacement button a shade darker than the others, Jamie folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing when listening.
life: “I keep stray mittens sorted by school because the children change stop every term.” People around Ferris Deli know Jamie by a small Friday habit. Jamie asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
personality: Jamie treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Jamie lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
family: Benjamin Sun is Jamie’s younger cousin. Jamie asks before bringing somebody along. Benjamin can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The school photograph that travels*, Benjamin says, “I taught her to swim at Pier Beach. I didn't recognize the quiet uniformed girl with her hair dry.”

name: Ada Ellis
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
voice: I gave directions using the old stop. A stranger arrived late for a reunion and I want to write to the host.
agenda: To send proper directions to the visitor who missed the reunion.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a washed violet jersey and a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf. Ada has an aquiline nose and a square chin, with short black hair swept back. Ada folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing during a conversation.
life: “I sold shoe polish from a crate before the stall had a roof.” On Monday, near the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, Ada checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
personality: Ada is good at starting things, dreadful at waiting for them to take effect. Close family can tell how worried Ada is by the number of tiny errands suddenly being done.
family: Jody Thomas is Ada’s cousin raised in the same household. Ada makes room at the table. Jody brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The other side of the cove*, Jody says, “I am hoping for a quiet place to feed my baby.”
connections: Gareth Arrieta. They trade better directions for the warning sound that once timed the morning toast.

name: Gareth Arrieta
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
voice: I listen for the doors before putting toast down. Now I burn it every morning and blame the council.
agenda: To get toast and shift time back into sensible order.
appearance: Gareth has fine brows over wide-set eyes. Look for short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. Out of work clothes, the familiar outfit is a cropped bottle-green coat with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. In conversation Gareth looks toward the door whenever a name is called.
life: “Night nursing taught me which breakfast places keep the lights low.” Sunday often includes a stop at Juniper Street, where Gareth knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
personality: Gareth tells a better story in a kitchen than at a microphone. Family members sometimes underestimate how far Gareth will go to back a quiet opinion once it is actually challenged.
family: Daryl Akers is Gareth’s half-sibling. Gareth saves a place. Daryl chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The clean ledger*, Daryl says, “I learned to read in prison. My own name on that page was the first word I didn't want to see.”

name: Stella Hull
voice: My wheelchair fits the new turn. I brought the planners cake and asked them to hear the old riders too.
agenda: To preserve the easier wheelchair turn and hear the displaced riders.
appearance: Stella has brown hair pinned away from the temples, one cheek that creases before the other, and a favorite piece of clothing, an unlined tan jacket. It usually goes with a small enamel bird on the lapel. When somebody else has the floor, Stella holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
life: “I first measured pavement slopes with a marble and a plumb line.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the brick passage off the shop row, where Stella takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
personality: Stella is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Stella asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
family: Dario Flint is Stella’s second cousin. A relative kept reporting household news on postcards long after everybody could afford to phone. Reading one takes the family back to an ordinary morning rather than a big event. Stella saves apparently unimportant details. Asked about *A tide at noon*, Dario says, “I let children freeze the turrets in my cart.”
connections: Alicia Nielsen. An old-stop regular walks the new wheelchair turn alongside its advocate. Also in the story is Lou Arnett (route planner).

name: Teal Holmes
home: the blocks north of the port
voice: I found a ring under the old shelter. The date inside matches a couple who used to catch separate buses.
agenda: To return the found ring to the right couple.
appearance: Teal is easy to recognize by silvery hair gathered at the nape and a round face with a pronounced chin. Usually dressed in a long navy raincoat with a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf, Teal looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry when listening.
life: “I repaired the original shelter after the wind tore off its timetable.” Saturday often includes a stop at the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, where Teal prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
personality: Teal is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
family: Eden Song is Teal’s younger cousin. Teal keeps the photographs. Eden knows which ones can be shared. They enjoy remembering people in public and also know what it feels like to have a private afternoon turned into an anecdote for strangers. Asked about *Reading the payslip*, Eden says, “I found a pension contribution and called my father.”
connections: Nelson Carbone. The empty coffee corner finally has an errand for the person who found the ring.

name: Bianca Sethi
voice: I wrote the verse about my dad and then decided nobody gets to hear it yet.
agenda: To decide personally if the private verse will ever be heard.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a cream pullover and a train token tied to a zipper pull. Bianca has a round face with a pronounced chin, with thick, tightly coiled hair. Bianca gives a little nod before asking a hard question during a conversation.
life: “I first wrote lyrics in the backs of permission slips nobody returned.” People around Maré Coffee know Bianca by a small Wednesday habit. Bianca likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
personality: Bianca keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. Bianca wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
family: Samuel Choi is Bianca’s older relative by marriage. Bianca remembers the birthdays. Samuel asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The widow's dividend*, Samuel says, “I found a pencil debt to my mother between two lines about roofing nails.”
connections: Annette Alder (choir director). The conductor and writer agree who controls the unsung verse.

name: Marina Bly
home: the blocks north of the port
voice: I bought concert tickets for grandparents who expected a solo. I need to explain why silence is still a performance.
agenda: To help the grandparents understand their ticket bought a child's whole performance.
appearance: Marina has a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Look for short black hair swept back. appearance: Wesley has auburn hair cut square at the nape, a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, and a favorite piece of clothing, a faded indigo overshirt. life: “I signed prayers with Gran long before I could spell their opening words.” On Friday, near the window at Night Shift Donuts, Wesley knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
personality: Wesley has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Wesley knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
family: Gavin Roche is Wesley’s first cousin once removed. Wesley puts the kettle on. Gavin chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The guarantee*, Gavin says, “I processed the loan in six minutes and spent an hour telling the family how that was possible.”
connections: Maeve Hamm. Signing in the pause makes room for a listener who heard the fountain underneath it.

appearance: Lucinda has short black hair swept back, a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, a faded indigo overshirt. personality: Lucinda enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
family: Jorge Nash is Lucinda’s cousin raised in the same household. Lucinda chooses an ordinary story to tell. Jorge asks the question the rest of the family avoided. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *Laundry for a stranger*, Jorge says, “I thought my landlord paid for laundry. I want to repay the neighbor in a way she can decline.”
connections: Martin Martin. The accompanist's foot tapping stays on the recording along with the held breath.

name: Thomas Silva
voice: I hear the dryers through my pillow. I want one morning when the neighbors sing with them.
agenda: To agree one undisturbed morning with the singers.
appearance: Away from the heat of the kitchen, look for a red windbreaker and a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. Thomas has full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, with brown hair pinned away from the temples. Thomas touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word during a conversation.
life: “I still remember rocking a borrowed pram with my ankle.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the downtown fountain, where Thomas keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
personality: Thomas finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
family: Quinn Laurent is Thomas’s older cousin. Thomas calls about good news first. Quinn is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The day sailor's divorce*, Quinn says, “I kept hearing who paid most. I brought the maintenance log with everyone's cold hands in it.”

name: Russell Hooper
voice: My baby sleeps only during the spin cycle. The regulars saved the gentlest machine for us.
agenda: To save a gentle cycle for the baby's naps.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a black overshirt with pearl buttons and a narrow brass watch set a little fast. Russell has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, with a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow. Russell looks toward the door whenever a name is called during a conversation.
life: “I still remember my baby's first nap through the bakery alarm.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the steps at Pier Beach, where Russell watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
personality: Is a careful borrower and a reckless lender. Things leave this person's house with elaborate instructions and very little expectation of ever coming back.
family: Nolan Costa is Russell’s older relative by marriage. Russell is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Nolan calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *Saturday keys*, Nolan says, “I memorized which doors stick because I couldn't read the old tags.”

name: Irene Baptiste
voice: I put three different loads in to test my theory and dyed my best shirt.
agenda: To replace the shirt without blaming the washers.
appearance: Irene has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow. Look for a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears. Away from the heat of the kitchen, the familiar outfit is a striped cotton shirt with a train token tied to a zipper pull. In conversation Irene listens with the head tilted a little to the left.
life: “I still remember washing a restaurant apron until it turned pink.” On Wednesday, near Breakwater Way, Irene stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
personality: Irene is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. Irene loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
family: Mia Nair is Irene’s first cousin once removed. Irene offers the first invitation. Mia gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The clean ledger*, Mia says, “I want to be the last name he reads. I owe him an apology he never put in his ledger.”

name: Adrian Trent
voice: I remember a shipboard work song with the same interval. I came ashore to compare them.
agenda: To compare the seafarer's work song with the recording.
appearance: Adrian has a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Look for silver temples and a dark fringe. Back on the street, the familiar outfit is a charcoal zip cardigan with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. In conversation Adrian draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting.
life: “I still remember a bunkmate singing the same line three days straight.” On Tuesday, near the market by Market Flats, Adrian often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Adrian takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
family: Owen Brandt is Adrian’s younger cousin. Adrian asks the question the rest of the family avoided. Owen chooses an ordinary story to tell. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *A sail cut small*, Owen says, “I cut a pattern from the wrong edge and ruined my plan.”

appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a black overshirt with pearl buttons and a narrow brass watch set a little fast. name: Lucia Starr
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
voice: I wrote my first dance to those machines. I want to rehearse before customers start arriving.
agenda: To rehearse before opening without delaying work.
appearance: Lucia has auburn hair cut square at the nape, a heart-shaped face and prominent ears, and a favorite piece of clothing, a striped cotton shirt. It usually goes with a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. When somebody else has the floor, Lucia looks down for a moment before saying something difficult.
life: “I still remember rehearsing in a room with no mirrors.” On Friday, near the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, Lucia checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
personality: Lucia can be lavish with time and quite careful with cash. A free afternoon is sometimes the biggest gift Lucia can afford to give, and family knows to take it seriously.
family: Nelson Darzi is Lucia’s first cousin once removed. Lucia checks the date twice. Nelson brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *The carer's afternoon*, Nelson says, “I am the parent needing care. My daughter doesn't know I've wanted an afternoon without her questions too.”

name: Franklin Brandt
voice: I wanted the noisy bearing replaced. Hearing the song hasn't changed my mind about my night shift.
agenda: To buy one quiet night before the next shift.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an olive canvas jacket and a small enamel bird on the lapel. Franklin has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, with close-cropped dark curls. Franklin draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting during a conversation.
life: “I still remember the first night an entire ward slept.” Wednesday often includes a stop at Paper & Pine Books, where Franklin starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
personality: Franklin carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
family: Lou Arnett is Franklin’s stepsibling. Franklin chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Lou brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The sheltered corner*, Lou says, “I set the distance in a planning office. My father made me walk it with his groceries.”

name: Edgar Joseph
voice: I draw the alley bins because my mother knows cities by their cats.
agenda: To draw the city's working cats for family.
appearance: Edgar has black hair twisted into a small knot, a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a plum-colored cardigan. It usually goes with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. When somebody else has the floor, Edgar turns fully toward the person speaking.
life: “I still remember painting shadow cats on my first locker.” Saturday often includes a stop at the foot of Harbor Viaduct, where Edgar pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
personality: Edgar is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Edgar asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
family: Rain Yang is Edgar’s cousin raised in the same household. Edgar leaves the first voice message. Rain calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The new language at dinner*, Rain says, “I speak his language but the agency only knows I clean offices.”
connections: Hank Fry. An onboard drawing gives the souvenir seller an alternative to the hotel view.

agenda: To send the child a crane-shadow photograph.
appearance: Anton is easy to recognize by close-cropped dark curls and a narrow face with an expressive upper lip. Usually dressed in a long navy raincoat with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring, Anton counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices when listening.
life: “I still remember waiting through unloading with a blanket around two shoulders.” On Thursday, near the corner by Juniper Tailor, Anton looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
personality: Anton is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
family: Alex Carr is Anton’s cousin raised in the same household. Anton can always ask for five minutes alone. Alex asks before bringing somebody along. name: Ida Henry
voice: I bought a blank card to send my aunt the smell of her old soap.
agenda: To send the familiar scent without damaging the card.
appearance: Ida is easy to recognize by short black hair swept back and a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Usually dressed in a dark green knitted vest with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case, Ida gives a little nod before asking a hard question when listening.
life: “I still remember orange rind kept dry in my sea bag.” Tuesday often includes a stop at Harbour Bakery, where Ida buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
personality: Ida loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Ida remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
family: Idris Yeo is Ida’s cousin raised in the same household. Ida brings the paper and a pen. Idris decides what stays off the paper. They have helped each other make decisions that were far easier to discuss once the figures could be moved around. The decisions themselves still belong to the person asking. Asked about *The misplaced umbrella*, Idris says, “I stitched the patch from a dress my aunt wore on her only holiday.”
connections: Nora Ray. They compare how little room a parcel needs to carry the idea of home.

appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a moss-green cardigan and a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. Iris has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, with short black hair swept back. Iris presses the lips together to keep a smile in during a conversation.
life: “I still remember my first roll of film exposed through a torn pocket.” People around the corner outside Coastal Barber know Iris by a small Tuesday habit. Iris usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
personality: Iris finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
family: Luis Soto is Iris’s stepsibling. Iris remembers the birthdays. Luis asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *A civilian apology*, Luis says, “I was a probationer then. I kept quiet because the man signing the note was my mentor.”

life: “I still remember a letter arriving on the wrong continent.” People around the foot of Harbor Viaduct know August by a small Saturday habit. August pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
personality: August keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. August wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
family: Patricia Ramos is August’s younger relative by marriage. August offers the first invitation. Patricia gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The late crossing*, Patricia says, “I used to get lifts from my boss until I felt I couldn't refuse overtime.”
connections: Lee Murphy. A folded boat reaches one grandchild while a dance-hall print finds an old partner.

name: Nora Ray
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
voice: I wrote my address on the picture side because the picture looks more like home than my address does.
agenda: To get the home address on the preferred side of the picture.
appearance: Nora has a round face with a pronounced chin. Look for black hair twisted into a small knot. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a faded indigo overshirt with a thin silver ring worn on a cord. In conversation Nora touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word.
life: “I still remember moving with every possession in a flimsy bag.” Friday often includes a stop at the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, where Nora checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
personality: Nora always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Nora is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
family: Bailey Solis is Nora’s stepsibling. Nora puts the kettle on. Bailey chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *A scar at the salon*, Bailey says, “I can retouch it away. I offered a print with no edits so the client could make the first choice.”
connections: Ida Henry. They compare how little room a parcel needs to carry the idea of home.

name: Lee Murphy
voice: I found our old dance hall in the background of a harbor print and sent it to my ex.
agenda: To mail the dance-hall scene to a former partner.
appearance: Lee has two white streaks in otherwise dark hair, a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, and a favorite piece of clothing, a plum-colored cardigan. It usually goes with a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. When somebody else has the floor, Lee raises one eyebrow long before saying yes.
life: “I still remember a ballroom door too narrow for our scenery.” People around the blocks below Foundry Lofts know Lee by a small Friday habit. Lee checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
personality: Lee has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Lee knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.

They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *A chair of one's own*, Conrad says, “I rent my chair and earn well. I never tell newcomers my partner pays our mortgage.”

name: Selena Roberts
voice: I work nights and never see a blue sky here. I drew the floodlights instead.
agenda: To draw the actual night shift lights.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a gray fisher's sweater and a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. Selena has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, with black hair twisted into a small knot. Selena looks down for a moment before saying something difficult during a conversation.
life: “I still remember the silence before the first floodlight ignites.” On Tuesday, near the bank steps, Selena takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
personality: Selena enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
family: Paz Harrow is Selena’s stepsibling. Selena brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Paz checks the date twice. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *A tide at noon*, Paz says, “My little brother still thinks his castle was disqualified because I didn't like it.”
connections: Harold Byrd. They send the night lights and the lunch receipt as two honest views from one shift. Also in the story is Iris Vidal (harbor photographer).

name: Harold Byrd
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
voice: I mailed a receipt for lunch. My family has been asking what an ordinary day costs.
agenda: To explain the cost of an ordinary crew lunch at home.
appearance: Harold has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Look for close-cropped dark curls. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a red windbreaker with a pen clipped inside the neckline. In conversation Harold rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
life: “I still remember a packet of foreign coins taped to the pantry door.” On Monday, near the window at Night Shift Donuts, Harold knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
personality: Harold has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Harold can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
family: Isabel Doyle is Harold’s cousin raised in the same household. Harold brings a spare shopping bag. Isabel chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *A summer marriage*, Isabel says, “I have been saving for a huge wedding. Hearing these two haggle over chairs has made me question mine.”
connections: Selena Roberts. They send the night lights and the lunch receipt as two honest views from one shift.

name: Taylor Beck
voice: I want the first dividend in cash to tip the woman who cleaned our first office.
agenda: To give the first dividend to the original cleaner.
appearance: Taylor is easy to recognize by a neat white crop and a narrow face with an expressive upper lip. Usually dressed in a gray fisher's sweater with a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole, Taylor raises one eyebrow long before saying yes when listening.
life: “I still remember borrowing a refrigerator to cool the founders' lunch.” On Saturday, near Tideline Market, Taylor picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
personality: Taylor reads little signals of discomfort very accurately and has an unfortunate habit of overruling people for their own good. The friends who say stop are the ones Taylor trusts most.
family: Elaine Alcázar is Taylor’s younger relative by marriage. Taylor makes the call. Elaine is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *A dance for two fathers*, Elaine says, “I want my little girl to see grown men making room without one of them having to disappear.”
connections: Samuel Choi. They trace the first cleaner's tip back to an unpaid ledger line.

name: Rain Salcedo
voice: I had a silent share. My children still think my wealth came from my second husband.
agenda: To let the children hear about their mother's share.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a boxy denim jacket and a replacement button a shade darker than the others. Rain has a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones, with a gray streak running back from the forehead. Rain counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices during a conversation.
life: “I still remember an office key stamped with my maiden initials.” People around Paper & Pine Books know Rain by a small Saturday habit. Rain starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
personality: Rain has a quick wit and an equally quick sense of shame. A joke is often Rain's way of finding out whether a room is friendly enough for a serious question.
family: Nell Marks is Rain’s younger cousin. Rain can stop the walk at any corner. Nell chooses the familiar route. Walking side by side makes it easier to disagree without turning each disagreement into a contest. Asked about *The margin reader*, Nell says, “I'm translating the swear words first. They tell me where two polite people finally trusted each other.”
connections: Reuben Sawyer. A silent shareholder discusses what a child would gain from one small voting share. Also in the story is Samuel Choi (ledger reader).

name: Samuel Choi
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
voice: I found a pencil debt to my mother between two lines about roofing nails.
agenda: To settle the penciled debt to the mother.
appearance: Samuel has a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Look for a blunt cut just below the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a red windbreaker with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. In conversation Samuel looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry.
life: “I still remember the ledger balanced on an ironing board.” People around Juniper Street know Samuel by a small Thursday habit. Samuel knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
personality: Samuel listens for the familiar version of a story and then for the one detail that changes it. Friends bring problems here when they want to be heard twice.
family: Bianca Sethi is Samuel’s younger relative by marriage. Samuel asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Bianca remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The quiet verse*, Bianca says, “I wrote the verse about my dad and then decided nobody gets to hear it yet.”
connections: Taylor Beck. They trace the first cleaner's tip back to an unpaid ledger line. Also in the story is Rain Salcedo (founding shareholder).

name: Iva Allard
voice: I countersigned every page. The one missing signature is from the day I walked out.
agenda: To date the one unsigned ledger page.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an unlined tan jacket and a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. Iva has a wide brow and a narrow jaw, with a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow. Iva listens with the head tilted a little to the left during a conversation.
life: “I still remember practicing a signature in the back of a cab.” Monday often includes a stop at the window at Night Shift Donuts, where Iva knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
personality: Iva talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Iva's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
family: Maria Tanner is Iva’s second cousin. Iva brings the paper and a pen. Maria decides what stays off the paper. They have helped each other make decisions that were far easier to discuss once the figures could be moved around. The decisions themselves still belong to the person asking. Asked about *School after sixty*, Maria says, “I am the old class bully. The classmate I frightened has chosen the chair opposite me and asked me to keep quiet.”
connections: Daryl Trent. The missing signature makes the trustee ask whose stake the ledger didn't show.

That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. name: Grey Garza
voice: I forecast a loss and delayed moving home. One unexpected payment could bring my wife back to the coast.

appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a cream pullover and a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. Grey has a small notch in the left eyebrow, with a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow. Grey gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in during a conversation.
life: “I still remember confusing our birthday tape with a board meeting.” Saturday often includes a stop at the brick passage off the shop row, where Grey takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.

Asked about *A prize nobody entered*, Lane says, “I posted it because the author never took chances.”

They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *The soft wharf chalk*, Evelyn says, “I know the hook in that W from the attendance board.”

name: Reuben Sawyer
voice: I want one share for my grandson so somebody younger will keep asking how the rent is set.
agenda: To buy a share the grandson can responsibly vote.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an old plum windbreaker and a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. Reuben has a small notch in the left eyebrow, with a neat white crop. Reuben turns fully toward the person speaking during a conversation.
life: “I still remember the smell of a new envelope containing an old promise.” People around the corner outside Coastal Barber know Reuben by a small Thursday habit. Reuben usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
personality: Reuben uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Reuben well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
family: Gus Lark is Reuben’s cousin. Reuben chooses whether to use it. Gus saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The porch light*, Gus says, “I sold the owner two bulbs every winter. He always wrote my name in a little book beside the price.”

name: Hollis Parker
voice: I signed something blurry once. I brought my own glasses and stayed until she read every word.
agenda: To let the witness read every word at her own pace.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a dark green knitted vest and a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. Hollis has a small notch in the left eyebrow, with short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. Hollis draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting during a conversation.
life: “I still remember a council hearing where I mistook a four for a nine.” People around the entrance to the Wash House know Hollis by a small Tuesday habit. Hollis stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
personality: Hollis loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
family: Yusuf Solis is Hollis’s younger cousin. The household has two versions of an old recipe because somebody detested onions and never admitted it to the original cook. A person sitting down to eat gets to choose. Hollis will defend the changed version in front of purists. Asked about *One last dress rehearsal*, Yusuf says, “I play the villain. My dad has never seen me do anything at school except get in trouble.”

name: Jody Mehta
voice: I know that bent temple. I repaired it for my former partner after we split up.
agenda: To identify the old repair without involving the former partner unnecessarily.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a pale blue work shirt and a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. Jody has an aquiline nose and a square chin, with a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape. Jody rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket during a conversation.
life: “I still remember mending a pair of spectacles with fishing line.” On Tuesday, near the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio, Jody notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
personality: Jody enjoys routines and will defend the right of someone else to break one. As a result, Jody is often everyone's favorite cover for a missed morning.
family: Amanda Kerr is Jody’s half-sibling. Jody makes the call. Amanda is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. name: Quinn Carvalho
voice: I read the statement aloud too fast. I asked her to tell me where to breathe.
agenda: To record the witness's phrasing where the form allows it.
appearance: Quinn is easy to recognize by dark brown curls cut close behind the ears and a round face with a pronounced chin. Usually dressed in a long navy raincoat with a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining, Quinn holds eye contact until the other person has finished when listening.
life: “I still remember a witness asking me to pronounce their job correctly.” Monday often includes a stop at the corner outside Coastal Barber, where Quinn usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
personality: Quinn is cheerful on a bad morning and unexpectedly melancholy after a success. Finishing a hard thing means losing the daily company of the people who worked on it.
family: Agnes Kramer is Quinn’s half-sibling. Quinn leaves the first voice message. Agnes calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The upstairs lease*, Agnes says, “My aunt collects the rent. I told the tenants before offering to help with their figures.”
connections: Billie Warren (community interpreter). They turn the printed account into language the witness will actually sign.

voice: My market stall sells cheap frames. I want a basket of new pairs where witnesses can reach.

appearance: George is easy to recognize by a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape and a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. life: “I still remember a customer paying half now and half after the harvest.” On Thursday, near the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, George prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
personality: George finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
family: Dale Lloyd is George’s cousin. George chooses the familiar route. Dale can stop the walk at any corner. Walking side by side makes it easier to disagree without turning each disagreement into a contest. Asked about *The upstairs lease*, Dale says, “I took the larger bedroom after the divorce.”
connections: Dario Allard. The father's glasses help test the new reading basket at the desk.

voice: I thought her hesitation meant doubt. She could describe the room exactly once the letters stayed still.
agenda: To ask what the witness can see before judging hesitation.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a washed violet jersey and a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining. Alan has a wide brow and a narrow jaw, with thick, tightly coiled hair. Alan squares up pieces of paper while thinking during a conversation.
life: “I still remember being misheard across an echoing gym.” People around the corner by Juniper Tailor know Alan by a small Friday habit. Alan looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
personality: Is a careful borrower and a reckless lender. Things leave this person's house with elaborate instructions and very little expectation of ever coming back.
family: Sasha Watts is Alan’s stepsibling. Alan brings the paper and a pen. Sasha decides what stays off the paper. They have helped each other make decisions that were far easier to discuss once the figures could be moved around. The decisions themselves still belong to the person asking. Asked about *The absent signature*, Sasha says, “I married into the family after she left. I'd like to know why there isn't a single photograph of her on the quay.”

agenda: To let a diner borrow reading glasses without fuss.

life: “I still remember my dad rubbing prices off his own menu.” Friday often includes a stop at Studio Boulevard, where Dario waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
personality: Dario is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. Dario loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
family: Evelyn Wade is Dario’s older cousin. Their family had a rule about visiting someone who had fallen on hard times. Bring enough food for the next day and bring a reason for an ordinary conversation. Dario knows when a neighbor would rather come over than receive visitors. Asked about *The salon on strike*, Evelyn says, “I have savings. I promised to cover a day's wages for the youngest worker if she wanted to speak.”
connections: George Stahl. The father's glasses help test the new reading basket at the desk.

personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Geraldine takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.

name: Elise Kapoor
home: the blocks north of the port
voice: I drew the scene instead of spelling it. The witness moved the desk six inches on paper.
agenda: To produce a drawing the witness can correct.
appearance: Elise has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw. Look for dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a narrow-striped sweater with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring. In conversation Elise leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations.
life: “I still remember drawing directions for the person who found my bag.” Sunday often includes a stop at the foot of Harbor Viaduct, where Elise pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
personality: Elise can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
family: Remy Stowe is Elise’s stepsibling. Elise knows which ones can be shared. Remy keeps the photographs. They enjoy remembering people in public and also know what it feels like to have a private afternoon turned into an anecdote for strangers. Asked about *Window seven*, Remy says, “Those eight minutes belonged to a patient waiting for a scan.”
connections: Noel Holmes. A drawing of the room gives the hesitant witness a less public way to begin.

personality: Billie can be lavish with time and quite careful with cash. A free afternoon is sometimes the biggest gift Billie can afford to give, and family knows to take it seriously.

They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *Winter afloat*, Morgan says, “I built boats before I sold expensive moorings.”

home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
voice: I sat beside her because my own witness statement had cost me a friend. This time she chose when to sign.

appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a black overshirt with pearl buttons and a watch on a cracked leather band. life: “I still remember an usher who set his chair beside mine.” On Saturday, near the blocks below Foundry Lofts, Noel checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
personality: Noel carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
family: Katherine Lowe is Noel’s younger cousin. Noel asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Katherine remembers the birthdays. name: Grey Ibrahim
voice: I used her kitchen as my savings bank when I sold pills. It's the only clean rent record I have.
agenda: To get a dated rent receipt the old neighbors recognize.
appearance: Grey has thick, tightly coiled hair, fine brows over wide-set eyes, and a favorite piece of clothing, a pale blue work shirt. It usually goes with a small enamel bird on the lapel. When somebody else has the floor, Grey turns fully toward the person speaking.
life: “I still remember earning a landlord's trust one damp banknote at a time.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the downtown fountain, where Grey keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
personality: Grey tells a better story in a kitchen than at a microphone. Family members sometimes underestimate how far Grey will go to back a quiet opinion once it is actually challenged.
family: Lou Khan is Grey’s cousin raised in the same household. Grey chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Lou brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The bitter orange*, Lou says, “She ordered two slices after her husband died.”

name: Tariq Banks
voice: My envelope held money for driving lessons. I was too embarrassed to say I failed again.
agenda: To save for another honest attempt at the driving test.
appearance: Tariq is easy to recognize by a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears and fine brows over wide-set eyes. Usually dressed in a red windbreaker with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip, Tariq counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices when listening.
life: “I still remember three attempts at the same blind corner.” Wednesday often includes a stop at Maré Coffee, where Tariq likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
personality: Tariq is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Tariq asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
family: Daniel Morris is Tariq’s older relative by marriage. Tariq keeps the photographs. Daniel knows which ones can be shared. They enjoy remembering people in public and also know what it feels like to have a private afternoon turned into an anecdote for strangers. Asked about *The soft wharf chalk*, Daniel says, “I was supposed to wash the underside. My wrists gave out halfway through and spared the words.”

agenda: To recover the paper bearing the late wife's handwriting.
appearance: Graham has one cheek that creases before the other. Look for a long silver braid. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a long navy raincoat with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. In conversation Graham looks down for a moment before saying something difficult.
life: “I still remember the stationery my wife ordered just to write rent checks.” On Wednesday, near Breakwater Way, Graham stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
personality: Graham is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
family: Pat Garrett is Graham’s cousin. Graham makes the call. Pat is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *A prize nobody entered*, Pat says, “I kept a diary nobody read for sixty years.”

name: Reina Gallagher
voice: I collected rent in the rain and swapped the tins. I traced every tenant before closing my books.

name: Remy Morris

voice: I calculated the turn perfectly and forgot the banister finial my grandmother carved.
agenda: To measure the carved finial with the family present.
appearance: Remy has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow. Look for a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a brown corduroy jacket with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. In conversation Remy draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first.
life: “I still remember measuring a doorway twice and a fresco once.” Monday often includes a stop at the entrance to the Wash House, where Remy stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
personality: Remy tells a better story in a kitchen than at a microphone. Family members sometimes underestimate how far Remy will go to back a quiet opinion once it is actually challenged.
family: Sylvia Kang is Remy’s cousin raised in the same household. Remy keeps the photographs. Sylvia knows which ones can be shared. They enjoy remembering people in public and also know what it feels like to have a private afternoon turned into an anecdote for strangers. Asked about *Three minutes at the bridge*, Sylvia says, “I manage payroll and discovered our time clock rounds those exact three minutes away in one department.”
connections: Penelope Hong. They measure a carved obstacle before moving the piano again.

name: Alexei Taylor
home: the ground floor of a Midtown walk-up
voice: I rent the ground floor. I asked for lessons in exchange for living with somebody else's piano.
agenda: To exchange room in the flat for lessons.
appearance: Alexei has a small notch in the left eyebrow. Look for short black hair swept back. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a soft blue checked shirt with a replacement button a shade darker than the others. In conversation Alexei steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
life: “I still remember my landlady teaching me the loud pedal.” People around the market by Market Flats know Alexei by a small Sunday habit. Alexei often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
personality: Alexei is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Alexei asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
family: Anthony Bell is Alexei’s older cousin. Alexei makes the call. Anthony is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The rescue hut mural*, Anthony says, “I sell postcards from the wrong angle and people prefer them.”
connections: Lena Osborne (piano owner). The owner and the ground-floor tenant have to agree on lessons as well as rent.

name: Kit Porter
voice: I played scales while the adults argued. By the time they stopped, I could play with both hands.
agenda: To learn the landing tune with both hands.
appearance: Kit is easy to recognize by short copper curls and a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Usually dressed in a charcoal zip cardigan with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip, Kit draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting when listening.
life: “I still remember drumming on every tall step before school.” People around the downtown fountain know Kit by a small Sunday habit. Kit keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
personality: Kit is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
family: Rowan Armas is Kit’s stepsibling. A lost family paycheck once turned up in the lining of a coat. Their relatives still describe that week by the three people who quietly extended credit. Kit would rather forgive a debt than make a friend cross the street. Asked about *The misplaced umbrella*, Rowan says, “I wanted an elegant beach photograph. The patch in the background is the one thing my mother recognized.”
connections: Amanda Hart. A breakfast listener gives the child an unhurried first audience.

name: Silas Watts
voice: I wanted to cut a new door. The downstairs tenant offered the piano a room of its own.
agenda: To agree a ground-floor home for the piano.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a gray fisher's sweater and a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. Silas has an aquiline nose and a square chin, with short copper curls. Silas turns fully toward the person speaking during a conversation.
life: “I still remember fitting a window for a neighbor's parrot.” On Saturday, near the corner outside Coastal Barber, Silas usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
personality: Silas loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Silas remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
family: Selena Lin is Silas’s cousin raised in the same household. Silas chooses the familiar route. Selena can stop the walk at any corner. Walking side by side makes it easier to disagree without turning each disagreement into a contest. Asked about *The kitchen without a boss*, Selena says, “I am the ill owner. I rang to find out what burned and for once three people refused to tell me.”
connections: Terry Acosta. They weigh the damaged maker's name against the cost of a new door.

name: John Collins
voice: I heard the landing concert from the street. I've given the household the recording of its reluctant orchestra.
agenda: To deliver the impromptu concert to the upstairs family.
appearance: John has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow. Look for a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape. life: “I still remember hearing someone whistle my first composition.” On Monday, near the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, John prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
personality: John has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
family: Teal Ruiz is John’s first cousin once removed. John brings the paper and a pen. Teal decides what stays off the paper. They have helped each other make decisions that were far easier to discuss once the figures could be moved around. The decisions themselves still belong to the person asking. Asked about *The last home visit*, Teal says, “I always asked for the window shut because my partner felt the cold.”
connections: Ivy Knight. A street recording lets the neighbor compare how the bass sounds outside.

name: Nadia Hayes
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
voice: I learned sums selling tomatoes. I ran the paper till and earned my first paid shift.
agenda: To earn a first paid shift on the counter.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an olive canvas jacket and a small enamel bird on the lapel. Nadia has a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, with a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow. Nadia steadies a cup with both hands while listening during a conversation.
life: “I still remember my mother totaling a stall's takings in song.” On Monday, near the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, Nadia prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
personality: Nadia has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Nadia knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
family: Jo Johnson is Nadia’s cousin raised in the same household. Nadia checks the date twice. Jo brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *Level with the window*, Jo says, “I delivered a complaint and a cake to the same desk.”
connections: Nadia Holland. Drawings and mental arithmetic keep the lunch queue moving.

name: Marlowe Paige
voice: I put down too much money to avoid looking broke. The cashier brought my change to work.
agenda: To settle the deliberate overpayment in private.
appearance: Marlowe is easy to recognize by close-cropped dark curls and a heart-shaped face and prominent ears. Usually dressed in a long navy raincoat with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread, Marlowe touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word when listening.
life: “I still remember needing the price of a stamp before payroll.” People around the bank steps know Marlowe by a small Saturday habit. Marlowe takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
personality: Marlowe enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
family: Lennon Sanders is Marlowe’s half-sibling. Marlowe brings a spare shopping bag. Lennon chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The day sailor's divorce*, Lennon says, “I teach their son. His favorite part of Sunday is actually the walk to breakfast afterward.”

name: Cian Malik
voice: I recognized my first boss's pencil shorthand. I can read the tab nobody else understands.
agenda: To read the shorthand on the oldest tab.
appearance: Cian has black hair twisted into a small knot, a wide brow and a narrow jaw, and a favorite piece of clothing, a moss-green cardigan. It usually goes with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. When somebody else has the floor, Cian squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
life: “I still remember shorthand drawn in the flour on a worktop.” Friday often includes a stop at the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio, where Cian notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
personality: Cian has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Cian can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
family: Malcolm Tan is Cian’s second cousin. Cian asks before bringing somebody along. Malcolm can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The fountain score*, Malcolm says, “I brought an empty milk tin from the shop my parents lost.”

personality: Billie takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Billie can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.

Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *A chair of one's own*, Rowan says, “I offered two days a week instead of six. I have a sick partner and I know exactly what three empty days cost.”

life: “I still remember a jammed drawer my mentor opened with patience.” On Saturday, near Ferris Deli, Duncan asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
personality: Duncan admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Duncan learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
family: Silas Rubio is Duncan’s cousin. Duncan saves a place. Silas chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The release address*, Silas says, “I own the shop he robbed. My own kids know him only as the man who sends birthday cards.”

Asked about *The carer's afternoon*, Emilio says, “I owned a care agency and thought four hours was simple.”

name: Michael Hubbard
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
voice: I watched through a shop window on my break. The drummer came inside and finished the song for me.
agenda: To bring the next shop colleague out to hear the ending.
appearance: Michael has a round face with a pronounced chin. Look for short black hair swept back. Away from the heat of the kitchen, the familiar outfit is a pale blue work shirt with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. In conversation Michael folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing.
life: “I still remember listening to park concerts behind the loading door.” People around the corner by Juniper Tailor know Michael by a small Saturday habit. Michael looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
personality: Michael has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
family: Sofia Cruz is Michael’s half-sibling. Michael saves a place. Sofia chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *A civilian apology*, Sofia says, “I can still hear the call from that day. The caller described a red door and we all heard red coat.”
connections: Anthony Carey. The repaired stool goes to the shop for a brief last song.

name: Riley Fox
voice: I was the usual replacement and nobody called. I played the tambourine until the jealousy passed.
agenda: To offer percussion support without trying to reclaim the stool.
appearance: Riley is easy to recognize by a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape and two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Usually dressed in an old plum windbreaker with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial, Riley presses the lips together to keep a smile in when listening.
life: “I still remember a substitute who played my part beautifully.” Tuesday often includes a stop at Studio Boulevard, where Riley waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
personality: Riley treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Riley lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
family: Nia Brooks is Riley’s cousin raised in the same household. Riley picks the meeting place. Nia sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The Saturday swap*, Nia says, “I need to sing at a funeral. The man we're burying once complained about my conduct, and he was right.”
connections: Samuel Drew (regular drummer). The original drummer promises the overlooked substitute a private rehearsal.

name: Ren Trent
voice: I kept the invitation because I want to offer my chair at the orchestra rehearsal the same way.
agenda: To pass the orchestra chair to a willing guest.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a soft blue checked shirt and a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. Ren has a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, with short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak. Ren turns fully toward the person speaking during a conversation.
life: “I still remember the smell of rosin above worn rehearsal carpets.” Saturday often includes a stop at Breakwater Way, where Ren stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
personality: Ren is good at starting things, dreadful at waiting for them to take effect. Close family can tell how worried Ren is by the number of tiny errands suddenly being done.
family: Ingrid Kaur is Ren’s older relative by marriage. A relative left a box of miscellaneous screws beside a perfectly labeled set of good tools. The box was the first thing the family fought over after the funeral. Ren remembers who needs to be asked before the repair. Asked about *A room above the dryers*, Ingrid says, “I can fit a sink if the room is used after school one evening a week.”
connections: Esther Mills. The old invitation helps an orchestra librarian make a new, personal one.

name: Oakley Han
voice: I want it lined in cold blue like the restaurant I used to run.
agenda: To host a Sunday dinner in the blue-lined coat.
appearance: Oakley has a gray streak running back from the forehead, full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, and a favorite piece of clothing, a pale blue work shirt. It usually goes with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. When somebody else has the floor, Oakley starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak.
life: “I still remember a waiter ironing my sleeves before our first opening.” On Saturday, near Harbour Bakery, Oakley buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
personality: Oakley loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Oakley remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
family: Silas Voss is Oakley’s younger cousin. Oakley remembers the birthdays. Silas asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *A scar at the salon*, Silas says, “I wrote a manipulative slogan about survival and took it out before the presentation.”
connections: Noel Aubin (housecoat maker). They measure a garment for a whole Sunday, including sitting at the head of the table.

name: Hugo Paul
voice: My partner left me three silk ties. They're becoming the pockets she specifically asked for.
agenda: To turn the late partner's ties into real pockets.
appearance: Hugo has a loose dark braid, a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a gray fisher's sweater. It usually goes with one cuff folded back twice. When somebody else has the floor, Hugo gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in.
life: “I still remember my widowed aunt refusing to throw away neckties.” On Wednesday, near the bank steps, Hugo takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
personality: Hugo finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
family: Sam Collins is Hugo’s cousin’s child. Hugo knows which ones can be shared. Sam keeps the photographs. Asked about *A wall of birthdays*, Sam says, “I put the marks on transparent paper so families who rent can take their years with them.”

name: Max Clay
voice: I bought washable cloth and lied about the price. She made me bring back the receipt.
agenda: To agree the actual cloth price with the client.
appearance: Max is easy to recognize by a long plait tucked inside the collar and a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Usually dressed in a gray fisher's sweater with a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining, Max looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry when listening.
life: “I still remember my first expensive silk ruined by cheap soap.” On Wednesday, near the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, Max prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
personality: Max keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. Max wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
family: Grant Tran is Max’s half-sibling. Max chooses an ordinary story to tell. Grant asks the question the rest of the family avoided. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *One last dress rehearsal*, Grant says, “I usually photograph every performance. I put the camera away because the mother wanted her face to be private.”

name: Alice Brooks
voice: I painted her nails to match before the cloth came. Now we have to laugh about two different reds.
agenda: To find a nail shade that works with the different red.
appearance: Alice has dark brown curls cut close behind the ears, a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, and a favorite piece of clothing, a mustard canvas overshirt. life: “I still remember filing a chipped nail in a bus shelter.” People around Lighthouse Cove know Alice by a small Saturday habit. Alice takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
personality: Alice always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Alice is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
family: Javier Rahman is Alice’s first cousin once removed. Alice checks the date twice. Javier brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *Summer staff*, Javier says, “I sold my van to afford the cart permit. I'm asking the council whether the permit can follow me inland.”

appearance: Felix has an aquiline nose and a square chin. Look for dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. life: “I still remember getting invited into the dining room after washing up.” Thursday often includes a stop at the corner by Juniper Tailor, where Felix looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
personality: Felix has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Felix knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
family: Scout Marin is Felix’s older cousin. Felix brings a spare shopping bag. Scout chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *Winter afloat*, Scout says, “I can offer a sofa but my son needs a place to come back to when he's sober.”

name: Darcy Hardy

life: “I still remember disliking my nickname long before I learned its origin.” On Tuesday, near Maré Coffee, Adrian likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.

voice: I walked an elderly man home under the wrong umbrella. That's where we found the right owner.
agenda: To walk the umbrellas to their correct owners.
appearance: Carlo has a small notch in the left eyebrow. Look for dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a boxy denim jacket with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring. In conversation Carlo holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
life: “I still remember sharing one umbrella along a street with six awnings.” Friday often includes a stop at the brick passage off the shop row, where Carlo takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.

family: Kai Kohli is Carlo’s older cousin. Carlo chooses the familiar route. Kai can stop the walk at any corner. Walking side by side makes it easier to disagree without turning each disagreement into a contest. Asked about *The driving lesson fund*, Kai says, “I used to be a cabdriver. I am teaching map reading in the park while the fund grows.”

name: Franklin Pike
voice: I offered boxes and got asked to be a witness at the lease meeting. I'm wearing my good shoes for that.

name: Simon Hunter
voice: I have nine hours on that sheet and a refrigerator full of food I bought on credit.
agenda: To recover the nine hours before the grocery tab is due.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a mustard canvas overshirt and a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. Simon has a heart-shaped face and prominent ears, with thick, tightly coiled hair. Simon listens with the head tilted a little to the left during a conversation.
life: “I still remember a week's overtime written on a damp matchbook.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the entrance to the Wash House, where Simon stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
personality: Simon has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
family: Melanie Nelson is Simon’s half-sibling. Simon decides what stays off the paper. Melanie brings the paper and a pen. They have helped each other make decisions that were far easier to discuss once the figures could be moved around. The decisions themselves still belong to the person asking. Asked about *The clean ledger*, Melanie says, “I am the creditor everyone thought dead. I'm asking for an afternoon of help moving house.”

voice: I ran payroll. I warned management on Wednesday and told the crews on Friday. I can't get Thursday back.
agenda: To tell the crew exactly when management got the warning.
appearance: Bruna is easy to recognize by auburn hair cut square at the nape and two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Usually dressed in a striped cotton shirt with a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges, Bruna rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket when listening.
life: “I still remember the morning a payroll transfer stopped halfway through.” People around the window at Night Shift Donuts know Bruna by a small Saturday habit. Bruna knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
personality: Bruna always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Bruna is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
family: Anton Dove is Bruna’s half-sibling. Bruna can always ask for five minutes alone. Anton asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *Window seven*, Anton says, “Window seven is the first place I saw the sea after I moved here.”
connections: Penelope Jeong. The manager's daughter hears which day the payroll worker knew about the shortfall. Also in the story is Simon Hunter (freight worker).

People at home learned to ask for the collapsed one first so the baker could sit down. Penelope thinks it tasted better with the icing in the middle. Asked about *A four o'clock kitchen*, Francis says, “I was asking for cheaper coffee before I learned the cook was paying someone to wake her youngest.”

name: Charles Shah
home: the blocks north of the port
voice: I managed their books through both pregnancies. I want the years of unpaid work named before anyone divides the money.
agenda: To record the years of unpaid work.
appearance: Charles has iron-gray waves, a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, and a favorite piece of clothing, a plum-colored cardigan. It usually goes with one cuff folded back twice. When somebody else has the floor, Charles counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
life: “I still remember doing two salaries' worth of work on one pregnancy.” People around Juniper Street know Charles by a small Sunday habit. Charles knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
personality: Charles is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
